content.text:
Silhouette: Horizontal brown bear frame carried on two hind legs, European rhinoceros beetle wings in place of the forelegs, jointed tail segments in place of the tail. Host frame: the brown bear sets the outline, body size and overall frame. A single creature combining a European rhinoceros beetle and a brown bear. Head of the brown bear, fully visible and uncluttered, with clear, discernible eyes. Details: limbs with thick supporting legs and visible breathing openings along the flanks; European rhinoceros beetle jointed tail segments in place of the tail; tail as signature part of the second parent; European rhinoceros beetle exoskeleton in a few large patches over the forequarters and neck, at full strength with clean edges, color and surface unchanged inside each patch; brown bear coat everywhere else; behavior follows the head donor; plain coat with no stripes or spots; European rhinoceros beetle wings in place of the forelegs, standing on two hind legs; wings held for display or gliding, not powered flight. Coat texture flows along the body outline. Declared fiction: arthropod parts at large size, shown with thick supporting legs and visible breathing openings along the flanks. Bilaterally symmetrical with recognizable limbs and visible sense organs. Habitat cue (grassland): dark back and light belly with strong countershading. Prosaic detail: natural lighting, feet in firm contact with the ground with a soft shadow, normal wear on hooves, claws and skin. One creature, full body, side three-quarter view, plain light background, natural history illustration.
Aspect ratio: 1:1.

summary.text:
**Designing hybrid creature concept**
I'm shaping a single creature that uses a brown bear's horizontal frame and head with clear eyes, swapping the forelegs for European rhinoceros beetle wings and the tail for jointed beetle segments, plus thick hind legs and visible flank breathing openings.
**Researching beetle anatomy details**
I'm looking up European rhinoceros beetle reference images to capture wing shape, exoskeleton texture, and spiracle placement for the hybrid illustration.
**Generating beetle anatomy image**
I'm creating the illustration using the reference, with dark brown elytra, membranous wings as forelegs, and visible spiracles for accurate beetle anatomy.
**Refining beetle wing design**
I'm adjusting the concept to a single pair of wings and removing the extra exoskeleton plates for a cleaner anatomy, then preparing to generate the updated image.
